newsitem.title: USA: Estrogen therapy said to benefit elderly women.
newsitem.headline: Estrogen therapy said to benefit elderly women.

text.p: It may never be too late for older women to begin taking oestrogen to combat bone density loss that leads to osteoporosis and fractures, researchers said on Tuesday.

A study of 740 women aged 60 to 98 found that those who began oestrogen therapy after the age of 60 achieved a bone mineral density similar to women who began taking the hormone right after menopause.

Oestrogen is generally believed to be most effective way to prevent and treat osteoporosis in postmenopausal women but there has been disagreement over when the therapy should start and concerns about breast cancer with long-term use, the study said.
Osteoporosis is the loss of protein tissue from the bone, which causes it to become brittle.

"These data provide some of the strongest evidence to date that oestrogen therapy should be continued into late life for the maintenance of high bone density," said the study from the University of California, San Diego.
"Estrogen begun after age 60 years appears to offer remarkably similar bone density benefit to oestrogen begun in early menopause or after (removal of ovaries)..." the study said.

"If late continuous use is equivalent to early onset continuous use, oestrogen therapy could be initiated at older ages when most osteoporotic fractures occur, reducing the cost and possible risks of long-term oestrogen therapy," it added.
The study, published in this week's Journal of the American Medical Association, said more research was still needed on the subject.
